findings.title: Possible TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Many callers now pass `[]` (cancel, confirm, payment webhooks, bookingReminder), and handleNewBooking may pass `null`. A Meet-located event with no destination calendar will therefore throw instead of falling back to Cal Video. It needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: evt.destinationCalendar can be null so team calendars are silently dropped, and the array can be mutated
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so teammates' calendars are never added for a COLLECTIVE event. In that case the organizer gets the fallback calendar while the team members' calendars are skipped. The array literal also only holds one element, and pushing mutates it after the event has been built. Initialise to `[]` and concatenate instead.

findings.title: If the event type has its own destinationCalendar, the organizer's calendar is ignored
findings.body: When `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, the array becomes `[eventType.destinationCalendar]` and the organizer's own destination calendar is never included. Team members' calendars are then appended after it. The fallback semantics are confusing and may leave the organizer's own calendar un-invited for collective events.

findings.title: createEvent picks the destination calendar by credentialId only, falling back to 'primary'
findings.body: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents also calls `createEvent` for entries that have no credentialId (matched by integration type) and for the fallback and other_calendar paths. In those cases Google can create the event on the credential's primary calendar rather than the intended destination. Previously the single destination calendar's externalId was always used. This is a behaviour regression for destination calendars without a credentialId. In addition, the later `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined when only the 'primary' fallback was used, so the hangout-link patch fails.

findings.title: No-op find on externalCalendarId in updateEvent/deleteEvent
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only evaluates the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, so it never matches. The fallback is dead code and `calendarId` becomes undefined in `updateEvent`, whereas it previously fell back to the destination calendar's externalId.

findings.title: Duplicate events created: createEvent runs per destination with the full event
findings.body: When a destination has no credentialId, `createEvent` is called for every credential of that integration type for each destination. If several destinations share an integration type, the same credentials receive multiple creates, which produces duplicate events. The result list also mixes references with `externalId` undefined, so saved references lose their calendar id and updates and deletes may target the wrong calendar.

findings.title: updateEvent called with an undefined credential
findings.body: If `reference.credentialId` is set but neither the in-memory credentials nor the DB lookup yield a credential, `credential` stays `undefined` (or keeps the previous loop value). `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called anyway, which throws inside CalendarManager. The outer catch then discards every result. The old code had a similar shape, but a missing credential is now more likely because other hosts' credentials are referenced. Skip the reference when no credential is found.

findings.title: Error log removed in the catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was deleted, but `message` is still built. Failures in updateAllCalendarEvents are now swallowed with no logging, which makes debugging harder, and the `message` variable is left unused.

findings.title: Multi-host destination calendars not handled by Office365/Lark/CalDAV
findings.body: These services take only the first destinationCalendar (`mainHostDestinationCalendar`) and ignore `credentialId`. EventManager calls `createEvent` once per destination with the same full event. With a collective event where several hosts use the same provider, each credential's service creates the event in the main host's calendar id, which is wrong for the other hosts. The Office365 `deleteEvent` and `updateEvent` are also unchanged.

findings.title: Unrelated rewrite of loadUsers changes behaviour and drops the organization select
findings.body: The `loadUsers` rewrite removes the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` select for dynamic users, which later code may rely on. It also throws when `dynamicUserList` is empty and wraps any error into a 500 'Unable to load users'. This is an out-of-scope behaviour change that is hard to review in a PR about destination calendars.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of org slug logic
findings.body: The old code set `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` when billing was enabled. The new code sets `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, which flips the behaviour. With billing enabled the org slug is now set immediately, before payment or verification, and without billing no slug is set at all. This is unrelated to the PR and looks like a bug.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is used for the broken calendar name
findings.body: Only the first element of `destinationCalendar` is used, so a failure on another host's calendar would report the wrong integration name. This is also an arguably acceptable fallback, but it is undocumented.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId for results without it
findings.body: `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` is now taken from the result. `updateEvent` in CalendarManager does not set `externalId` or `credentialId` on its result, so references created via `updateLocation` (calendar updates) get an undefined externalCalendarId where they previously got the destination calendar's externalId. Stored references lose their calendar id.

findings.title: E2E expectations inconsistent and no tests added for the new multi-destination behaviour
findings.body: Only BOOKING_REJECTED was changed to expect `[]`, while the other webhook tests still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. No unit or e2e tests cover the new multi-host collective flow, even though the PR says no tests were added.
